old_caption: The video captures a serene beach scene at sunset. The sun is positioned low on the horizon, casting a warm golden glow across the sky and reflecting off the calm ocean surface. The sky is partially cloudy, with streaks of light breaking through the darker clouds, adding depth to the scene. The beach is sandy and appears relatively empty, with gentle waves lapping against the shore. On the right side of the frame, there is a cliff with a house perched on top, silhouetted against the bright sky. The house has multiple windows and a flat roof, blending into the natural landscape. The overall atmosphere is tranquil and peaceful, with the soft light creating a soothing ambiance. There are no visible animals or people in the scene, emphasizing the quiet beauty of the moment. The camera remains stationary throughout the video, allowing viewers to fully absorb the stillness and tranquility of the beach at sunset.

caption: The video captures a calm sea at dusk under a heavy gray sky, the low sun near a flat horizon and throwing a bright vertical column of light across the dark water. A steep cliff topped by a pale building anchors the right, while a pebbly shoreline sweeps diagonally through the foreground. The water moves throughout the scene. Small ripples travel across the surface, so the sun's reflection continuously shimmers, fragments, and reforms in a shifting glittering path. Along the right-hand shore, thin white foam shifts and reshapes the waterline. The sea's overall texture keeps changing without any large surge or splash arriving or ending. The cliff, building, horizon, and sun hold nearly fixed positions, suggesting little or no camera movement. The cloud masses show no clearly resolvable drift, holding their positions overhead. A small dark object near the right waterline stays roughly in place as the foam moves around it.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
